name: Y Combinator
position: Launch fast, talk to users, and make something people want; weekly growth is the compass, and the founder stays engaged in the details as the company scales.

name: Lean startup
position: A startup is a search for a working business model: treat every plan as a hypothesis and test it on real customers before scaling anything.

name: Blitzscaling
position: In winner-take-most markets, speed to scale beats efficiency: accept risk, waste, fires left to burn, and stage-fit hires to reach dominant scale first.

name: Bootstrapper
position: A profitable, independent company at a sustainable pace is complete success: fund with revenue, keep the team small, charge real prices, and define the outcome yourself.

name: Effectuation
position: Expert entrepreneurs start from their means (who they are, what they know, whom they know) and commit only what they can afford to lose, co-creating markets rather than predicting them.

name: Contrarian
position: The valuable truths are the ones the consensus rejects: escape competition into monopoly, commit to a definite plan, and engineer distribution deliberately.

name: Classical
position: The market, management, and venture canon that predates the current playbooks: market size decides outcomes, dominate a beachhead before expanding, watch for disruption from below, and build the professional systems a scaled company runs on.

name: Craft
position: Product quality is the strategy: pick the few attributes that make the product great, get them exactly right for a narrow set of users, and hold off scaling until the market pulls.
